title: The symmetric algebra of a finitely presented module is a finitely presented algebra, generated by generators of the module
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $M$ an $R$-module, with symmetric algebra $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\operatorname{Sym}^n_R(M)$ and the inclusion $M=\operatorname{Sym}^1_R(M)\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$. (a) If $m_1,\dots,m_n$ generate $M$ as an $R$-module, then they generate $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ as an $R$-algebra. (b) If $M$ is a finitely presented $R$-module, then $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra (isomorphic to $R[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(g_1,\dots,g_m)$); and then for every finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak a\subseteq\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)$ the quotient $\operatorname{Sym}_R(M)/\mathfrak a$ is a finitely presented $R$-algebra.
